title: Standard progress note note from F1: every section written + planted facts recalled
hypothesis: The Standard progress note template produces a complete note that captures the session's key facts.

sections.title: Presentation
sections.html: Client presented for a 50-minute individual session, diagnosed with F41.0 Panic disorder. Client appeared engaged and cooperative, though reported a rough week involving a panic attack in public. Mood was anxious, and affect was congruent with reported distress.

sections.title: Session content
sections.html:
Client discussed experiencing a panic attack at a grocery store checkout line on Tuesday, reporting physical symptoms of a pounding heart and leaving the cart to walk out.

Client reported automatic thoughts during the incident, specifically stating, "I was going to pass out in front of everyone and they would think I was crazy." Client completed two out of three assigned thought records during the week. Client also reported poor sleep averaging four hours per night with early morning awakening around 3:00 AM, and noted starting a new medication prescribed by a primary care doctor two weeks ago: sertraline 50 mg, with initial mild nausea that has since resolved. Client discussed feeling dismissed by a sister's advice to "just push through it."

sections.title: Interventions
sections.html:
• Reviewed completed thought records and evaluated belief ratings, utilizing CBT.
  • Conducted psychoeducation on the peak and natural decline of anxiety sensations.
  • Administered interoceptive exposure by having the client spin in a chair for 30 seconds to intentionally elicit dizziness and tracked anxiety ratings pre- and post-exposure, utilizing CBT.

sections.title: Client response
sections.html: Client responded well to reviewing thought records, recognizing a significant drop in belief regarding the thought of passing out from 90% in the moment down to 40% at home. During the interoceptive exposure exercise, client initially rated anxiety at a 6 following the spinning, and observed that the sensations decreased to a 3 within two minutes. Client gained insight that bodily sensations can peak and pass without requiring escape. Client was hesitant to invite the sister to a session at this time.

sections.title: Risk assessment
sections.html: No risk indicators were reported. Client denied any thoughts of hurting self or of not wanting to be alive.

sections.title: Plan
sections.html:
• Complete thought records 3 times this week.
  • Practice the interoceptive spinning exercise once a day at home.
  • Conduct an in vivo exposure by returning to the grocery store on a quiet Saturday morning and staying until anxiety drops by half.
  • Next appointment scheduled for the same time next week.
